clusters.label: Text Summarization Objectives and Types
clusters.rationale: c77 candidates 001-006 all introduce foundational classifications and goals of text summarization from the same source section, including objectives, mono/multi-document, extractive/abstractive, indicative/informative, generic/user-oriented, and supervised/unsupervised. They form a coherent group about the taxonomy of summarization.

clusters.label: Summarization Processing Steps
clusters.rationale: c77 candidates 007-011 cover the steps in summarization processing: intermediate representation, sentence scoring, selection algorithms, reformulation, and compression rate. These are sequential or closely related sub-processes described in the same source section.

clusters.label: Extractive Summarization Example with Python
clusters.rationale: c77_pro_thinking_012 is a standalone practical example of extractive summarization using Python and NLTK. It is distinct from the theoretical concepts and not closely related to other candidates, so it forms its own cluster.

clusters.label: Extractive vs Abstractive Summarization and BERT-based Methods
clusters.rationale: c78 candidates focus on extractive and abstractive summarization methods, including BERT embeddings, K-medoid clustering, keyword extraction, GPT-2 fine-tuning, and data challenges. They share a common theme of modern NLP approaches for summarization.

clusters.label: UML Deployment Diagrams
clusters.rationale: c79 candidates all relate to UML deployment diagrams, including nodes, artifacts, relationships, and use cases. They form a self-contained set on a specific UML diagram type, unrelated to summarization or GitHub features.

clusters.label: ISO 25010 Software Quality Characteristics
clusters.rationale: c80 candidates cover the ISO 25010 quality model and its characteristics and sub-characteristics. They are tightly related and should be grouped to avoid fragmenting a single standard.

clusters.label: codemetrics Library Usage
clusters.rationale: c81 candidates describe the codemetrics library, including its purpose, dependencies, and usage examples. They form a distinct cluster about a specific Python tool for code metrics.

clusters.label: GitHub Platform Features (Copilot, Actions, Codespaces, Security, Projects, Reviews)
clusters.rationale: c82 candidates cover various GitHub features including Copilot, Actions, Codespaces, Advanced Security, Dependabot, Projects, and code review. They all relate to the GitHub platform but are distinct enough that they could be evaluated further. For clustering, we group them as they all originate from the same source and describe GitHub's capabilities.
